You are working for an event catering company that has been hired to plan a corporate team building event menu for 30 people. Your task is to design a complete catering plan and get client approval.

Use the HowToCook recipe database to browse recipes across different categories. Select at least 8 dishes to create a full catering menu with appetizers, main courses, and at least one dessert or soup. Choose recipes that would work well for a corporate team building setting serving 30 people.

Create an Excel workbook called Catering_Plan.xlsx in your workspace with two sheets. The first sheet must be named Menu and include the columns Dish_Name, Category (use values like Appetizer, Main_Course, Soup, or Dessert), Servings_For_30 (the number of servings needed to feed the 30 guests, which is approximately 30 — one serving per guest — scaled up from the recipe's default serving count), Prep_Time_Minutes (estimated preparation time as a number), and Estimated_Cost_USD (estimated cost in US dollars as a number, estimate $3-8 per serving for most dishes). Write all numeric values (Servings_For_30, Prep_Time_Minutes, Estimated_Cost_USD, and any quantities) as literal numbers, not Excel formulas. The Menu sheet should have at least 8 data rows. The second sheet must be named Ingredients and include the columns Dish_Name, Ingredient, Quantity_For_30_People, and Unit.

Create a Word document called Catering_Proposal.docx in your workspace. Include an executive summary describing the event and your catering approach, a menu overview section listing all selected dishes with brief descriptions, and a preparation timeline section describing when each category of dish will be prepared on the event day.

Create a Google Form called "Menu Approval Survey" with questions to collect client feedback on the proposed menu. Include at least three questions: one asking the client to rate overall menu satisfaction, one asking which dishes they want to confirm or remove, and one asking for any special dietary requirements or additional notes.

Send an email to client@corporate.com with subject "Catering Proposal for Team Building Event" that summarizes the proposed menu and mentions that the Excel plan, Word proposal, and feedback form have been prepared.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Make one bounded category-discovery pass, select exactly eight suitable dishes covering appetizers, main courses, and at least one soup or dessert, and retrieve those eight recipe details with native-parallel calls. Freeze one eight-dish table and reuse it everywhere. Create `Catering_Plan.xlsx`, `Catering_Proposal.docx`, and the Form `Menu Approval Survey` as independent output branches. The workbook must use the exact two sheets and headers, literal numeric values, `Servings_For_30` values scaled to approximately 30, positive costs, and ingredient rows referencing the same dish names. Build the Word document with one bulk structured body containing the exact title, Executive Summary, Menu Overview, and Preparation Timeline and mentioning at least four exact selected dish names. Create the Form exactly once with these three explicit questions: `Rate the overall menu satisfaction from 1 to 5`; `Which dishes should we confirm or remove?`; and `List any special dietary requirements or additional notes`. Verify each deliverable once, then send exactly one email to `client@corporate.com` with subject `Catering Proposal for Team Building Event`.

Create a Word document at exactly this path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-howtocook-event-catering-excel-word/workspace/Catering_Proposal.docx

Use the word MCP tools (mcp__word__create_document, mcp__word__add_heading, mcp__word__add_paragraph, and mcp__word__add_table if helpful). Build the document with the following structure and content (write professional, complete sentences):

TITLE (Heading 1): Catering Proposal — Corporate Team Building Event
Subtitle paragraph: Prepared by [Your Catering Company] | 30 Guests | Buffet-Style Chinese Menu

SECTION 1 (Heading 1): 1. Executive Summary
Paragraphs covering: This proposal presents a complete catering plan for a corporate team building event for 30 people. The menu was designed using recipes from the HowToCook open-source recipe database, curated for group dining: crowd-pleasing classics, balanced nutrition, and dishes that hold up well when served buffet-style. The menu comprises 11 dishes across four categories — 3 appetizers, 5 main courses, 1 soup, and 2 desserts — scaled from each recipe's default serving size up to 30 servings (one serving per guest). Estimated cost ranges from $3–8 per serving per dish, and estimated preparation times are provided so the kitchen can plan staffing. A full ingredient list scaled for 30 people accompanies the plan in the Excel workbook (Catering_Plan.xlsx).

SECTION 2 (Heading 1): 2. Menu Overview
Intro paragraph: The following dishes were selected from the HowToCook recipe database. Each dish is listed with a short description and its category.

Use a table (Dish | Category | Description) with these 11 rows, OR headings + paragraphs per dish. A table is preferred for readability:
1. 凉拌黄瓜 (Cold Cucumber Salad) | Appetizer | Crunchy smashed cucumber tossed with garlic, vinegar, soy sauce and sesame oil — a refreshing, light starter that is quick to prepare.
2. 口水鸡 (Saliva Chicken) | Appetizer | Tender poached chicken chilled and dressed with a spicy, numbing chili-oil sauce with peanuts and cilantro — a classic Sichuan cold appetizer.
3. 凉拌木耳 (Cold Wood Ear Mushroom Salad) | Appetizer | Blanched wood ear mushrooms in a tangy garlic-chili dressing — crisp, healthy and easy to scale for large groups.
4. 宫保鸡丁 (Kung Pao Chicken) | Main_Course | Stir-fried chicken with roasted peanuts, scallions and dried chilies in a sweet-sour sauce — a universally popular main course.
5. 糖醋里脊 (Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin) | Main_Course | Crispy pork tenderloin coated in a glossy sweet-and-sour sauce — a crowd favorite that travels well for buffets.
6. 麻婆豆腐 (Mapo Tofu) | Main_Course | Silken tofu in a savory, mildly spicy sauce with minced pork and Sichuan pepper — a comforting, budget-friendly main.
7. 白灼虾 (Poached Shrimp) | Main_Course | Whole shrimp gently poached with scallion, ginger and wine, served with a soy-ginger dipping sauce — light, elegant and protein-rich.
8. 蒜蓉西兰花 (Garlic Broccoli) | Main_Course | Blanched broccoli florets finished with a garlicky soy-oyster sauce — a colorful vegetable main that balances the menu.
9. 玉米排骨汤 (Corn & Pork Rib Soup) | Soup | A hearty slow-simmered soup of pork ribs, sweet corn and carrot — a warming, comforting first course for the team.
10. 烤蛋挞 (Baked Egg Tarts) | Dessert | Flaky pastry shells filled with silky egg-custard and baked until golden — a crowd-pleasing dessert that is easy to portion.
11. 提拉米苏 (Tiramisu) | Dessert | Classic no-bake Italian dessert of mascarpone cream, coffee-soaked ladyfingers and cocoa — a rich finish to the meal.

SECTION 3 (Heading 1): 3. Preparation Timeline
Paragraphs describing when each category is prepared on event day (write 4-6 paragraphs, e.g.):
- 2–3 days before: Prepare dessert components — bake the egg tarts and assemble the tiramisu (it needs 4 hours minimum chilling), then refrigerate; marinate/dry-marinate nothing yet; place dried wood ear mushrooms to soak plans and order all produce.
- Day before (evening): Blanch and chill the wood ear mushrooms; pre-cook and chill the poached chicken for 口水鸡; cut vegetables; make the chili-oil dressing; start the soup base by parboiling ribs; prep marinades for the meat mains.
- Event morning (approx. 3 hours before service): Start the Corn & Pork Rib Soup simmering (it needs ~60 minutes); marinate the Kung Pao chicken and sweet & sour pork; poach the shrimp; cook the garlic broccoli.
- 1.5–2 hours before service: Prepare cold appetizers (assemble 凉拌黄瓜, plate 口水鸡 with sauce, dress 凉拌木耳); begin deep-frying the sweet & sour pork and stir-frying the mains.
- 30 minutes before service: Finish all hot mains and keep warm in chafing dishes; plate desserts; set up the buffet line in order: appetizers, soup, mains, rice, desserts.
- During service: Replenish dishes as needed and keep hot items above 60°C for food safety; reserve some portions of each dish for late arrivals.

Close with a short closing paragraph: The full ingredient quantities scaled for 30 guests are provided in Catering_Plan.xlsx. We welcome your feedback through the Menu Approval Survey and will adjust the menu based on your confirmation and any dietary requirements.

After creation, verify the document exists and extract its text with mcp__word__get_document_text to confirm all three sections are present. Report the file path and a summary of sections as your final deliverable.

You are handling the external client-facing steps for a catering proposal. Complete exactly two actions:

ACTION 1 — Create a Google Form:
Use mcp__google_forms__create_form with:
- title: "Menu Approval Survey"
- description: "Thank you for reviewing our catering proposal for the corporate team building event (30 guests). Please share your feedback on the proposed menu so we can finalize the plan."

Then add these questions to the created form (capture the returned formId):
Q1 (mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question, required=true): title "How satisfied are you with the proposed menu overall?" options: ["Very Satisfied", "Satisfied", "Neutral", "Dissatisfied", "Very Dissatisfied"]
Q2 (mcp__google_forms__add_checkbox_question, required=true): title "Which dishes would you like to REMOVE from the proposed menu? (Leave unselected dishes confirmed for the event)" options: ["凉拌黄瓜 (Cold Cucumber Salad)", "口水鸡 (Saliva Chicken)", "凉拌木耳 (Cold Wood Ear Mushroom Salad)", "宫保鸡丁 (Kung Pao Chicken)", "糖醋里脊 (Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin)", "麻婆豆腐 (Mapo Tofu)", "白灼虾 (Poached Shrimp)", "蒜蓉西兰花 (Garlic Broccoli)", "玉米排骨汤 (Corn & Pork Rib Soup)", "烤蛋挞 (Baked Egg Tarts)", "提拉米苏 (Tiramisu)", "None — keep all dishes"]
Q3 (mcp__google_forms__add_text_question, required=true): title "Do you have any special dietary requirements or additional notes?"

ACTION 2 — Send an email:
Use mcp__emails__send_email with:
- to: client@corporate.com
- subject: "Catering Proposal for Team Building Event"
- body (plain text, include ALL of the following content): a summary of the proposed menu (state it is a buffet-style Chinese menu for 30 guests with 11 dishes: 3 appetizers — Cold Cucumber Salad, Saliva Chicken, Cold Wood Ear Mushroom Salad; 5 main courses — Kung Pao Chicken, Sweet & Sour Pork Tenderloin, Mapo Tofu, Poached Shrimp, Garlic Broccoli; 1 soup — Corn & Pork Rib Soup; 2 desserts — Baked Egg Tarts, Tiramisu), mention estimated cost of $3–8 per serving, and explicitly state that the following have been prepared and are ready for your review: (1) the Excel catering plan (Catering_Plan.xlsx) with menu and ingredient details, (2) the Word proposal (Catering_Proposal.docx) with executive summary, menu overview and preparation timeline, and (3) the "Menu Approval Survey" Google Form for feedback. Ask the client to complete the survey so the team can finalize the menu. If you can obtain the form's shareable URL from the form-creation response, include it in the email; otherwise reference the form by name.

Report back: the Google Form ID and title, the three questions added, the email recipient/subject, and confirmation that the email was sent (including any email/message ID returned).
